preamble: The velar nasal [ŋ] is replaced by the glottal fricative [h] in the Huastecan branch of Mayan: Proto-Mayan *ŋ appears as h in Huastec word-finally, so that Proto-Mayan *q'iiŋ 'sun, day' corresponds to Huastec k'ih, *ʔooŋ 'avocado' to ʔuh, and *laajuuŋ 'ten' to laajuh. The change removes both nasality and oral place of articulation. Other Mayan branches have x (K'iche'an–Mamean) or n (Q'anjob'alan, Cholan, Yucatecan).

examples.note: Chicomuceltec also has k'ih; Huastec tak'in 'silver, money' with -n is therefore explained as a loan from a lowland Mayan language.

sources: Kaufman, T. (2003). A Preliminary Mayan Etymological Dictionary, pp. 460, 1109, 1481. FAMSI. https://www.famsi.org/reports/01051/pmed.pdf
Norcliffe, E. (2003). The Reconstruction of Proto-Huastecan. MA thesis, University of Canterbury. https://glottolog.org/resource/reference/id/109784
